key_insight: Frequency-division multiplexing lets superconducting qubits share microwave gate-control lines, with a proposed framework targeting 10–100× fewer lines.
engineering_relevance: Shared control wiring could ease dilution-refrigerator wiring-density and cooling-power constraints as quantum processors scale.
method: Combine gate-control signals into polychromatic microwave pulses.
Use band-pass filters to address frequency-separated control channels.
Integrate multiplexed gates with microwave readout and on-chip DC sources in a periodically extensible architecture.
evidence_signal: A 1:4 demonstration achieved average parallel-gate errors of (6.4 ± 0.2) × 10⁻³ for CZ and (10.6 ± 0.2) × 10⁻⁴ for XY(π/2), with no statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation.
watch_item: The projected 10–100× line reduction remains to be validated at larger scales, where frequency crowding, crosstalk and filter integration may constrain performance.
paper_title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
